sources.title: British Museum: Western Xia authority record
sources.note: Institutional chronology, 1038 to 1227, and synonyms Western Xia, Tangut and Xixia. Used only state identity and dates; imported map warnings derive from decoded repository features in identities.json.

sources.title: UNESCO: Xixia Imperial Tombs
sources.note: Original World Heritage entry: 1038 founding, 1227 Mongol conquest, Ningxia heartland, multicultural population, funerary remains. Pooled conservatively with ICOMOS evaluation for source-word budget.

sources.title: ICOMOS: Evaluation of the Xixia Imperial Tombs, 2025
sources.note: Direct PDF pages 1 and 2: earth/brick/wood construction, nine royal mausoleums, 271 subordinate tombs and ancient flood protection comprising 26 dikes and six drainage ditches. Introductory 1032 founding conflicts with body and UNESCO 1038; public uses 1038. Drainage is funerary flood protection, not household sanitation.

sources.title: Jeongwon Hyun: Gift Exchange among States in East Asia during the Eleventh Century
sources.note: University of Washington dissertation, 2013. Original repository abstract verified in indexed text; direct page errors. Abstract explicitly identifies Xia strategic position in Central Asian trade and commercial benefits under Song return gifts. No numerical tribute totals or unverified treaty clauses used.

sources.title: Shi Jinbo, translated by Hansong Li: Tangut Contracts, in The Economy of Western Xia
sources.note: Open-access scholarly chapter, 2021, pages 262 to 523. Full indexed original text checked; direct Brill fetch fails. All passages and all mirrors pooled as one book. Land/houses/canals section 3.1.8.3 to 3.1.8.5, printed 384; wife co-borrower section 2.1.9.2, printed 309; employment section 5.1, printed 457 onward. Last-month 1219 contract governs nine months in 1220; translation Chen-year slip avoided.

sources.title: Nie Hongyin, National Library of China: Opening the door to Tangut writing through the Pearl in the Palm
sources.note: Direct scholar-authored library article dated 22 August 2017, excerpting his 2014 book. Gule Maocai 1190 bilingual dictionary, 37 leaves, butterfly binding, lotus filler decorations and possible Zhang private printer. Uncertain printer/location not asserted; no claim universal schooling or oldest bilingual dictionary.

sources.title: Andrew West: Tangut Coins, Da’an inscription and character references
sources.note: Direct primary epigraphic analysis, 29 January 2007, Unicode update 2017. Da’an row and clear-reading paragraph verify 𘜶 𗵐 𘏨 𘔭 with Chinese 大安寶錢, clockwise order and meaning. Author identifies other coin readings as uncertain, which are not used. Dates given broadly as late eleventh century; modern standardized transcription, not facsimile of a specific museum coin.

sources.title: National Museum of China: Currency catalogue, Da’an baoqian
sources.note: Original museum catalogue indexed text directly verified by query site:chnmuseum.cn 大安宝钱. Lists Western Xia example, diameter 2.4 cm and mass 3.4 g. Direct fetch inaccessible; no claimed visual inspection. Institutional attestation of object type complements West’s explicit reading.

sources.title: Shih-shan Susan Huang: Reassessing Printed Buddhist Frontispieces from Xi Xia
sources.note: Author-hosted full scholarly article, Zhejiang University Journal of Art and Archaeology 1 (2014), printed 123 onward. Printed 137 to 139 royal printing institutions and 1189 assembly; printed 151 Hongfo banner donor Zhao Zhong and family in Jin territory, dated 1190 to 1227. All three passages pooled under 200 words. No conflation with Jin-family donors on printed 152 to 153.

sources.title: Tang X L and Liu J Y: Tangut prescriptions for children’s head sores, 2016
sources.note: Original PubMed English abstract checked through indexed page; direct access recaptcha. Zhonghua Yi Shi Za Zhi 46(2), 103 to 110, DOI 10.3760/cma.j.issn.0255-7053.2016.02.008. Three prescriptions инв6476-28, 29, 30, Russian collection, Zhi re bing yao lun. No ingredient, efficacy, exact medieval manuscript year or universal access claim.

sources.title: British Library International Dunhuang Programme: Conservation and research of Tangut material
sources.note: Original indexed project text checked; direct 403. Stein third expedition 1913 to 1916, Khara Khoto material dated tenth to fourteenth centuries. Surviving collections span beyond independent Xia; not all texts are assigned to 1038 to 1227.

sources.title: International Dunhuang Programme: Multicultural Dunhuang and the Sulaiman stele
sources.note: Direct page, section after Mongol conquest in 1227: 1348 Sulaiman stele at Mogao, mantra in Sanskrit, Tibetan, Old Uyghur, Phagspa, Tangut and Chinese. Used only postconquest language continuity. Earlier 836 Tibetan Medicine Buddha painting on this page is not Western Xia evidence.

proposedOverrides.summary: The Tangut imperial state of Western Xia in western China, conventionally dated 1038 to 1227.

batchIdentityNotes.finding: Exact indexed name Xixia, imported 1000 to 1279, conventionally imperial Western Xia 1038 to 1227. No runtime or staged collision at claim. Three decoded snapshots have nearly identical wide footprints, bbox about 85.13 to 110.50 E and 37.74 to 42.12 N. Extent is not independently certified; chronology is demonstrably misleading before proclamation and after conquest and is publicly flagged. From/to retain map coverage. No aliasing to earlier Xia dynasty or modern Ningxia. Item 1348 explicitly postconquest continuity. Override omits fell and successors; preserve any curated transition.
